toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: EDF-2 analysis using initial evidence plus X11 (one catalogue item collected; stopped after it because it settled the main discriminating question).
output.brief:
What is going on: the rise is mostly a bag-tag problem, not a handling problem. Since 1 September, Corvane tags printed on the new Fennick Labels stock fail automatic reading about 11.8% of the time, against 1.5% for the old Brackwater stock. Counter-printed and kiosk-printed tags fail at similar rates. When counters briefly used Brackwater stock on 14–16 October, their failure rate fell to 1.6%, while kiosk tags issued the same days still failed at 12%. Other carriers' tags read normally on the same scanners, so the scanners are not the problem. Diverted bags then miss the 35-minute lateral closure.

How sure: moderately. The timing and the switch-back result are strong. Whether the fault is the stock itself or the printer heat setting is not settled, and I did not test the handler-crew or evening-bank explanations directly.

Next: switch counters and kiosks back to Brackwater stock now; it is valid to 31 December and about five weeks is in store. Test Fennick stock separately before any defect claim. Hold the breach notice: the data does not show Tessaly caused this, and the notice would penalise the wrong party. Consider a temporary evening encode workstation while the switch-back takes effect.
